cards.back: Forming a necessary base or core; of central importance. Example: 'Freedom of expression is a fundamental right in democratic societies.'
To produce or create something. Example: 'Solar panels generate electricity by converting sunlight into usable energy.'
To formally give or allow something, especially a right, permission, or funding. Example: 'The university granted scholarships to students who demonstrated exceptional academic performance.'
To provide a formal assurance that certain conditions will be fulfilled. Example: 'No teaching method can guarantee success without consistent effort from the learner.'
A system in which members are ranked according to relative status or authority. Example: 'The corporate hierarchy determines the chain of command within the organization.'
To draw special attention to something; to emphasize. Example: 'The report highlights the urgent need for investment in public transportation systems.'

A proposed explanation made on the basis of limited evidence as a starting point for further investigation. Example: 'The researchers tested their hypothesis by conducting a controlled experiment with two groups.'
To explain or make something clear by using examples, charts, or other visual aids. Example: 'The graph illustrates the steady increase in global temperatures over the last century.'
To put a plan, decision, or agreement into effect. Example: 'The school plans to implement a new curriculum that emphasizes practical skills.'
Implied though not directly expressed; understood without being stated. Example: 'There was an implicit assumption in the study that all participants had equal access to technology.'
To force something to be accepted or put in place, often by authority. Example: 'The government imposed strict regulations on carbon emissions from industrial facilities.'
Something that motivates or encourages someone to take a particular action. Example: 'Tax incentives were introduced to encourage businesses to invest in renewable energy.'
To include something as part of a whole; to take in or contain. Example: 'The revised textbook incorporates the latest findings from recent scientific research.'
To point out or show something; to serve as a sign of. Example: 'The survey results indicate a growing preference for online learning among university students.'
Certain to happen; unavoidable. Example: 'With continued population growth, some degree of environmental impact is inevitable.'
Existing as a natural or permanent quality of something. Example: 'There are inherent risks involved in any form of scientific experimentation.'
To hinder, restrain, or prevent an action or process. Example: 'Excessive noise in the classroom can inhibit students from concentrating on their work.'
To cause a process or action to begin. Example: 'The government initiated a nationwide campaign to promote public health awareness.'
To introduce new methods, ideas, or products. Example: 'Companies that fail to innovate risk losing their competitive advantage in the market.'
To combine one thing with another so they become a unified whole. Example: 'The curriculum aims to integrate theoretical knowledge with hands-on practical experience.'
To explain the meaning of information, words, or actions. Example: 'Different scholars may interpret the same historical event in very different ways.'
To carry out a systematic inquiry to discover and examine facts. Example: 'The team was appointed to investigate the causes of the recent decline in student enrollment.'
To cite or appeal to something as an authority or justification. Example: 'The defense attorney invoked the constitutional right to free speech during the trial.'
To set apart from others; to identify something separately. Example: 'Researchers were able to isolate the specific gene responsible for the inherited condition.'
To show or prove to be right, reasonable, or warranted. Example: 'The author uses statistical evidence to justify the claims made in the conclusion.'
Open to new ideas and willing to respect individual freedoms; not strict or rigorous. Example: 'The country adopted a more liberal approach to immigration policy in the early 2000s.'
In the same way; also or similarly. Example: 'Smoking has well-documented health risks; likewise, excessive alcohol consumption poses serious dangers.'
To discover the exact position of something or to be situated in a particular place. Example: 'The new campus is strategically located near major public transport links.'
To handle or control something in a skillful manner, or to influence someone unfairly. Example: 'Critics accused the media outlet of attempting to manipulate public opinion through biased reporting.'
Fully developed physically or mentally; having reached an advanced stage of growth. Example: 'Mature students often bring valuable professional experience to classroom discussions.'
A system of parts working together; a natural or established process. Example: 'The study examined the biological mechanisms by which stress affects the immune system.'
To move from one region or country to settle in another. Example: 'Millions of people migrate to urban areas each year in search of better employment opportunities.'
To reduce something to the smallest possible amount or degree. Example: 'Safety protocols are designed to minimize the risk of accidents in the laboratory.'
To make partial or minor changes to something. Example: 'The researchers modified their approach after the initial experiment produced inconclusive results.'
To observe and check the progress or quality of something over a period of time. Example: 'Environmental agencies continuously monitor air quality levels in major cities.'
In spite of that; nevertheless. Example: 'The evidence was limited; nonetheless, it provided a useful starting point for further research.'
A conception or belief about something. Example: 'The notion that intelligence is fixed has been challenged by recent research in neuroscience.'
Not influenced by personal feelings or opinions; based on facts. Example: 'Scientific research requires an objective analysis of data, free from personal bias.'
To counterbalance or compensate for something. Example: 'The increase in fuel costs was offset by greater efficiency in the production process.'
Continuing; still in progress and not yet completed. Example: 'There is ongoing debate among scientists about the long-term effects of microplastics on marine life.'
The final result or consequence of a process or action. Example: 'The outcome of the negotiations was a comprehensive trade agreement between the two nations.'
A typical example or pattern of something; a model or framework of thinking. Example: 'The discovery marked a paradigm shift in how scientists understood cellular biology.'
To become aware of or understand something through the senses or the mind. Example: 'The way individuals perceive risk can vary considerably depending on cultural background.'
To continue firmly in an opinion or course of action despite difficulty or opposition. Example: 'Gender disparities in pay persist in many industries despite decades of reform efforts.'
A particular attitude toward or way of regarding something; a point of view. Example: 'Studying abroad offers students a broader perspective on global issues and cultural differences.'
A fact or situation that is observed to exist or happen, especially one whose cause is in question. Example: 'Global warming is a well-documented phenomenon supported by extensive scientific data.'
Present as the strongest or main element; having the greatest influence. Example: 'English remains the predominant language used in international academic publications.'
To formally forbid something by law, rule, or other authority. Example: 'Several countries have enacted legislation to prohibit the use of single-use plastic bags.'
A part, share, or number considered in relation to the whole. Example: 'A significant proportion of the population now relies on the internet for daily news.'
A set of rules or procedures governing a formal process or system. Example: 'All clinical trials must follow strict ethical protocols to protect the rights of participants.'
To improve something by making small changes or removing impurities. Example: 'The author refined her thesis after receiving detailed feedback from her supervisor.'
To strengthen or support something, especially with additional material or evidence. Example: 'The findings reinforce the argument that early childhood education has lasting benefits.'
To prevent someone or something from doing something; to keep under control. Example: 'Financial regulations are intended to restrain excessive risk-taking by banks and investment firms.'
To continue to have or hold something; to keep possession of. Example: 'Students who review material regularly are more likely to retain information over the long term.'
To make previously unknown or secret information known to others. Example: 'The investigation revealed significant discrepancies between the reported and actual figures.'
To change something to its opposite direction, position, or course. Example: 'The new policy aims to reverse the trend of declining enrollment in science programs.'
To examine and make corrections or alterations to a piece of work. Example: 'Students should revise their essays carefully before submitting them for assessment.'
Unable to bend or be forced out of shape; strict and inflexible. Example: 'The rigid structure of the examination system has been criticized for stifling creativity.'
A postulated sequence or development of events; a possible situation. Example: 'Researchers modeled several scenarios to predict the effects of rising sea levels on coastal cities.'
The extent of the area or subject matter that something deals with. Example: 'The scope of the research was limited to the impact of social media on adolescent mental health.'
A particular order in which related events or things follow each other. Example: 'The experiment required participants to recall a sequence of numbers in the correct order.'
A slight change in position, direction, or tendency. Example: 'There has been a significant shift in public opinion regarding renewable energy sources.'
To imitate or reproduce the conditions of a situation or process. Example: 'Computer models can simulate the effects of natural disasters on urban infrastructure.'
Not likely to change or fail; firmly established. Example: 'A stable economy provides the foundation for sustained growth and social development.'
Uncomplicated and easy to understand or do. Example: 'The instructions for the assignment were straightforward and left little room for confusion.'
A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim. Example: 'The company developed a new strategy to expand its presence in emerging markets.'
To present a document, proposal, or application for consideration or judgment. Example: 'All dissertations must be submitted electronically by the end of the academic term.'
Coming after something in time; following. Example: 'The initial study and subsequent research both confirmed the link between diet and heart disease.'
Enough to meet the needs of a situation or a proposed end. Example: 'The student did not provide sufficient evidence to support the main argument of the essay.'
To strengthen or support something so that it continues over a period of time. Example: 'It is difficult to sustain economic growth without investing in education and technology.'
An objective or result toward which efforts are directed. Example: 'The government set a target to reduce carbon emissions by forty percent within the next decade.'
To make a thorough or dramatic change in form, appearance, or character. Example: 'Digital technology has transformed the way people access and share information.'
A general direction in which something is developing or changing. Example: 'The trend toward remote working has accelerated significantly since the pandemic.'
To experience or be subjected to something, typically something unpleasant or demanding. Example: 'All candidates must undergo a rigorous selection process before being admitted to the program.'
To make practical and effective use of something. Example: 'The research team utilized advanced statistical methods to analyze the survey data.'
